races.name: Dragonbet Welsh Racing Festival 9th-11th Oct Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Courseyoudo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Tom Lacey partnered by William Cox; 60 days off the track is the key flag here, and a form string of 6758 over good ground shows no win yet — soft conditions are untested and a gap from the back in a small field on 5f may never materialise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and 60 days absent, Courseyoudo nevertheless has experience over today's trip and carries a workable 135 lb from stall four, with our rating matching his official mark of 65 and positioning him as a genuine threat; the main risk is whether that layoff has left him ring-rusty.

runners_data.name: Crystal Kraken
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes over for Dylan Cunha's yard, who is in excellent form at 6/26 over 14 days; Crystal Kraken has run two consecutive seconds on good ground at 5f-6f and is the natural on-pace rival to Our Fella, making this a straightforward positional play if he jumps well.
runners_data.comment: Crystal Kraken has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second in each of her last two outings, and her experience over today's trip bolsters her claims as the one to beat; winless in her last six starts, she will need to convert that placed form, but at 131 lb from stall two, she looks the class act here.

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and carries headgear for J S Moore; trainer is 0/15 over the last 14 days which is worth noting, but sole pace control on a flat 5f in soft ground is a powerful structural advantage that overrides that concern.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and second three starts back, Our Fella arrives here fresh enough on 22 days' rest, has run over today's trip, and our rating of 68 marks him as a genuine threat; the risk is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Lion Of Persia
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's juvenile is lightly-raced with only three runs showing improvement (8-4-2) and his latest effort was a close second over 5f on good ground; a natural hold-up horse who will need the leaders to tire, and 47 days off the track adds a fitness query over the sharp 5f trip.
runners_data.comment: Lion of Persia shaped well when second last time out and has run over today's trip, while 131 lb from stall one adds a fitness query after 47 days off — the main risk for a gelding yet to score in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Naval Cop
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's yard is firing at 11/65 over 14 days and Alfie Redman (7) takes the ride, but Naval Cop is a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position because the rear is oversubscribed — his STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 signals he is unlikely to replicate his natural race shape, and his form of 465 over 5f-6f gives limited encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, Naval Cop faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and returns after 36 days, but her recent sequence of fifth, sixth and fourth offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Devon Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's runner ran only two days ago — the freshness concern is acute — and her form of 706364 is modest; she is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map, carries the lowest OR in the field at 45, and her sole soft-ground start produced a win in a sim-going filter (1/6) though that data point is thin and must be treated cautiously.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Devon Angel is hard to fancy despite returning just two days ago — though she has run over today's trip before and a third three starts back offers a crumb of form.

races.paceDynamic: Our Fella is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f nursery on Good to Soft ground at Chepstow, and with no rival likely to press him hard from the off, he should be able to roll along at a controlled, self-set tempo rather than be burned up in a speed duel. Crystal Kraken is the natural prominent type and will look to sit just off the heels of Our Fella, while the true hold-up horses — Courseyoudo, Lion Of Persia, Naval Cop and Devon Angel — will be strung out behind. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear; Naval Cop and Devon Angel are genuine come-from-behind horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map, but in reality they are likely to be last or nearly last and will need ground to open up that may not materialise. With a sustainable, uncontested gallop set by Our Fella on a soft surface that will reward those who race prominently and travel through the race rather than make up ground from deep, this shape strongly favours the lead and prominent profiles — particularly any horse close enough to pounce when Our Fella is collared late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Our Fella Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Our Fella breaks cleanly and Crystal Kraken is content to track rather than pressurise, Our Fella controls tempo and rations his effort across the full 5f on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Our Fella sets a measured pace that is hard to reel in from off the pace on testing ground, and Crystal Kraken, sitting handiest, is best placed to challenge if he fades but may also be outgunned if Our Fella stays on strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Our Fella's early fractions are just quick enough to expose him in the final furlong and Crystal Kraken or a close-stalking rival sweeps past.
scenarios.body: The soft ground stretches the field and the horse travelling most smoothly in second or third position arrives with the most momentum in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a rare gap opens for the genuine closers dropped out at the rear to deliver a late run.
scenarios.body: Courseyoudo or Lion Of Persia, racing from off the pace in a slowly-run 5f on soft ground, would need a messy finish and rivals to tie up dramatically to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Cop or Devon Angel, unable to get their natural rear position, find themselves forced wider and forward and strike a fortunate run through.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially less likely given both horses carry STYLE_FIT discounts and are racing out of their natural role, so any success would be incidental rather than tactical.

watchPoints.text: Our Fella carries the sole front-running role in a six-runner field — watch his gate start closely; if he misses the break Crystal Kraken could seize the lead and the entire race shape inverts.
Devon Angel ran just two days ago and Laura Coughlan (3) must manage a horse who may be ring-rusty or fatigued; watch for signs of her travelling laboured in the early stages.

Naval Cop and Devon Angel are both true hold-up types likely to be last away and last on the track — if the pace is slow and they get no gap through the field, they are likely to be unable to land a blow regardless of finishing ability.

The going report lists this race as Good to Soft, not Soft as declared — if the ground is better than expected, Our Fella's stamina reserves matter less and the overall pace may be sharper, compressing the field and making it harder for hold-up horses to find daylight.
Crystal Kraken's trainer Dylan Cunha is running at a strong 6/26 strike rate over 14 days — Rossa Ryan on a yard in form over the course-distance-going combination warrants monitoring in the market.

races.name: Eddie & Sandra Hayward Supports Noahs Ark Charity Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Anna Belardo
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in this field, giving her a clear lead to herself from the break; good-to-soft going is not a concern on her form and Ashley Lewis's 3lb claim is a small bonus, though her recent form figures of 7-6-3 show she is competitive without yet winning.

runners_data.name: Beechwood Glory
runners_data.note: John Butler's runner returns after 23 days in solid recent form (2-3-5 over this trip in good ground), but its natural hold-up style means it needs a truly honest pace to deliver — in this race, that pace is unlikely to materialise, and the more forward berth it will occupy dilutes its chance considerably.

runners_data.name: Conscientious
runners_data.note: Archie Watson has had good recent strike rate (2/20 over 14 days) but this horse's sole run produced a ninth and a notable tendency to fade in the finish, which is an obvious red flag on soft ground where stamina demands increase; hard to recommend at any stage of the race.

runners_data.name: Ischgl
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes the ride on the most experienced horse in the field, with two places from five runs on similar going (soft/good-to-soft) and a third over 7f in soft last time suggesting the conditions are no problem; a prominent style suits this race shape well and this looks the most straightforward fit of the prominent trio.

runners_data.name: Texas Crown
runners_data.note: William Carson's mount has placed twice on Fibresand but its sole turf run produced an eleventh on good ground, making the step up to soft turf a genuine unknown; a prominent style is right for today's race shape but the surface question tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Washington Royale
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs is an upgrade in the saddle for Michael Appleby's consistent but uninspiring 4-5-5 runner; three runs over this exact trip in good ground have all produced mid-division placings without threatening, and soft going is an untested variable, though the prominent style is correctly placed for today.

runners_data.name: Foxsbrush
runners_data.note: John Ryan's runner has shown nothing in two starts (10th and 7th over 6-7f on good ground), and as a hold-up type on a day when the pace is unlikely to be strong enough for late closers, the tactical situation compounds an already difficult profile to recommend.

races.paceDynamic: Anna Belardo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just three prominent types (Ischgl, Texas Crown, Washington Royale) likely to push forward into the early stages, she faces a manageable challenge for the lead on this flat Chepstow 6f in good-to-soft ground. The three prominent runners will jostle for position behind her, but none is a natural pace-pressurer capable of making Anna Belardo's lead untenable, so she is expected to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo rather than face a true war of attrition. On soft ground over a flat 6f, a measured gallop set by a front-runner who is not harried suits those who can track the pace and quicken late rather than deep hold-up types who need a truly strong pace to close into. This race shape distinctly favours prominent-to-tracking runners who can sit just off a controlled lead and pounce in the final two furlongs; the field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear and find the strong pace they need, with Beechwood Glory — a genuine hold-up horse — the most likely to be pushed out of its natural position and unable to produce its best from a more forward berth than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Anna Belardo gets a soft lead and the pace stays honest but uncontested, allowing prominent trackers to pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: Anna Belardo dictates a sustainable rhythm and the three prominent types Ischgl, Texas Crown and Washington Royale are ideally placed to strike approaching the final furlong; soft ground rewards those who have settled just off the pace rather than come from deep. This is the dominant shape in a race with one front-runner and several genuine prominent horses who should naturally slot into the chasing positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Anna Belardo is left completely uncontested and the soft ground suits her enough to sustain her advantage to the line.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace rival to test her early and the gallop controlled entirely to her liking, Anna Belardo could simply conserve enough energy to hold the prominent challengers at bay through the final furlong. Soft going does not categorically stop a well-placed front-runner from staying on if the pace has been judicious, and Rossa Ryan's Ischgl is the most likely to get closest without quite getting there.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent trio push Anna Belardo hard early enough to collapse the pace, creating a slow-burn finale that opens the door for hold-up types.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace on soft ground could produce a late scramble in which fresher legs coming from midfield catch the weakening leaders; Beechwood Glory is the obvious candidate but, having been displaced from its natural hold-up position, it may not settle far enough back to generate a meaningful late run. Foxsbrush also qualifies in style but its recent form figures (10, 7) give little reason for confidence even in a pace-collapse scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a slow break or traffic trouble causes the field to bunch in the straight, making position irrelevant and reducing the race to raw ability on the day.
scenarios.body: With seven runners on a flat 6f in soft ground, a bunched finish is possible if early positions are not cleanly established, giving any runner a theoretical chance; Washington Royale's consistency in placing suggests it would not be out of the mix in a muddled finish. This remains a low-probability fringe scenario dependent on unpredictable circumstances rather than the race pattern itself.

watchPoints.text: Anna Belardo is completely alone on the lead — watch whether the three prominent runners (Ischgl, Texas Crown, Washington Royale) apply any pressure in the opening furlong, because if they do not, she may dictate a dangerously slow pace that sets up her own winning chance.

Beechwood Glory is a genuine hold-up horse that will not get its preferred position in this race; watch whether Lewis Edmunds tries to hold it back against its likely forward momentum, as any positional compromise could further undermine its chance.

Texas Crown's jockey William Carson may be forced wide tracking the pace on a flat 6f course with a small field; soft ground and a wide draw could combine to cost this horse ground it cannot afford given its moderate turf form.

Conscientious is tagged as fading in the finish and has only one run to its name — watch whether it shows any early speed before dropping away, as its movement in the market could indicate whether connections believe the form reading is misleading.

Ischgl's experience advantage (five runs, two places on soft-type going) over several lightly raced rivals could be decisive if the race is run at a true pace; watch how confidently Rossa Ryan positions it in the first two furlongs as a signal of intended tactics.

races.name: Paving Fields Construction Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lucky Radar
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with OR=120 and no established running style, trained by Rod Millman who has a decent 14-day strike rate of 4/23; the unknown going and positional profile introduces genuine uncertainty, though Greatrex's booking suggests connections expect a forward showing.

runners_data.name: Flag Of Nations
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick runner carrying top weight of 131lbs alongside an OR=120 and no form string to analyse; Lewis Edmunds takes the ride and the horse's stylistic tendencies are entirely unknown, making this one of the hardest runners to place tactically in the race.

runners_data.name: Perola
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed pace-setter who has form at 6f on good-to-soft conditions and placed efforts on comparable surfaces; she is rated only OR=71 and racing out of her natural role in the sense that the STYLE_FIT flag tempers how much credit to give her chance if the race shape turns competitive — her value is as the race shaper, not necessarily the winner.

runners_data.name: Persian Gate
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's lightly-raced hold-up type whose only start produced a fifth over 6f on standard ground 15 days ago; Rossa Ryan is a strong booking and the horse's hold-up style is genuinely suited to running from off a slow pace, though generating momentum in soft ground off just one run is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Geemann
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's hold-up specialist has been repositioned in midfield on the pace map because this field cannot accommodate all its natural rear-dwellers; his sim-going record of 1 win from 8 on comparable surfaces and 0 place finishes in soft conditions is a meaningful concern, and his recent form of 0-0533 shows limited improvement — his true inclination is to come from off the pace, which this steady tempo may not reward.

runners_data.name: Kodicall
runners_data.note: J S Moore's runner has placed form at 6f on good ground and second at 6f on firm, stepping back to 6f after a fifth over 5f; a natural hold-up horse who will need the pace to collapse in the final furlong, which is unlikely given Perola's lone, measured front-running — Cox takes over in the saddle.

races.paceDynamic: Perola is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, she is expected to dictate a controlled, uncontested pace down the Chepstow straight on good-to-soft ground. That measured gallop from a single pace-setter creates a race where the fractions will not be punishing, meaning horses racing prominently behind Perola can travel well within themselves and pounce without the pace stringing the field out. Persian Gate, Kodicall and Geemann are all hold-up horses by nature, but with Perola alone in front and the race unlikely to be run at a searching tempo on this ground, closers will need to generate their own momentum rather than benefit from a hot early pace collapsing the leader. The race shape strongly favours horses that can race handy and travel smoothly into the contest — prominent-to-midfield profiles who can reel in Perola in the final two furlongs without needing a strong tempo to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Perola Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Perola bowls along uncontested and a prominent chaser reels her in inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Perola sets a measured tempo on soft ground and, having conserved energy, may stick on doggedly; however, a horse tracking closely and travelling strongly will have the edge if the pace is just steady enough to leave Perola vulnerable late. This shape rewards horses racing in the slipstream that can produce a clean, sustained finish over the final two furlongs on Chepstow's undulating straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Unknown Lightly-Raced Type Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed, lightly-raced entries produces a step forward in form to overpower the field.
scenarios.body: Lucky Radar or Flag Of Nations, both carrying OR=120 ratings and unknown unknown stylistic tendencies, could hold unexplored ability that renders the pace map largely academic; a physically maturing three-year-old who finds a rhythm on soft ground could sweep past the field in the final furlong. This scenario hinges entirely on untapped potential rather than predictable positional play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground produces a grinding test and true hold-up horses find sufficient late momentum.
scenarios.body: If the going proves more testing than the going report implies and Perola's steady pace still takes a toll, Persian Gate or Kodicall might close late from off the pace; however, with Geemann's recent record on good-to-soft ground unremarkable and Kodicall stepping back up in distance, this scenario asks genuine hold-up types to do real work generating their own pace. The soft surface could assist late finishers but the uncontested early tempo works against the late-charging profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Hands Race Away
scenarios.trigger: If Perola's early dominance comes at a cost and she stops sharply inside the final furlong handing the race to a late finisher.
scenarios.body: In the unlikely event Perola overcooks the pace from the front and ties up, any horse travelling well midfield or behind could inherit the race with minimal effort; however, given the small field and that Perola's form shows consistent placed efforts at this trip, total collapse is improbable. This scenario carries the lowest probability precisely because one controlled front-runner rarely burns out in a six-runner race on good-to-soft ground.

watchPoints.text: Perola's early tempo is the race's key variable — if she is allowed to roll at a comfortable clip unchallenged, horses trying to close from off the pace (Persian Gate, Kodicall) will struggle to generate the momentum needed on this soft ground.

Lucky Radar and Flag Of Nations are both OR=120 with unknown styles and lightly-raced profiles — either could outclass this field on raw ability alone if their initial runs understated their true level, making them impossible to fully discount.

Geemann's repositioning on the pace map means his shown midfield slot is not his natural position — watch for him to drift back towards the rear early, which in a small field over 6f on soft ground may leave him with too much ground to make up.

The going report lists this race as good-to-soft, notably softer than the official card input of soft — conditions are likely to favour horses with proven good-to-soft form (Perola, Kodicall) over those who have only raced on firmer ground.

With only six runners and a single front-runner, jockeys on hold-up horses may elect to push forward earlier than normal to avoid getting trapped in a slowly-run race — watch the early positions at the two-furlong mark to see if Rossa Ryan on Persian Gate tracks up closer than expected.

races.name: Runtech Ltd Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Prince Ali
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on soft ground earlier in the season and clearly handles cut, but Zoe Lewis claims 7lb and this 8-year-old's natural hold-up style has been pushed forward into midfield territory given the volume of closers in this field — his chance depends on a pace he may simply not get.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten into second two starts back and a winner three starts back, Prince Ali showed enough in recent starts to warrant respect, though a ninth last time out is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and his 131 lb burden from stall eight will test his stamina.

runners_data.name: Escape Magic
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has won twice at 7f on good ground for Owen Burrows; Rossa Ryan is a significant booking and the horse sets the tempo here with no meaningful rival, but the 37-day absence and first run on softer ground introduce an element of unknowing at a crucial moment.|
runners_data.comment: Escape Magic has two wins in her last five starts, including a winner two starts back, and third last time out keeps her firmly in the mix; she has run over today's trip before, though 37 days off and 130 lb from stall 10 are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Fullstop
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's three-year-old has run respectably in similar company and Ashley Lewis takes off a useful 3lb; a hold-up horse by nature whose best recent effort (third at 7f, good) gives some optimism, though the soft ground here is untested territory based on history.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked second in the field on our rating with a ten-pound pull on the official mark, Fullstop has run over today's distance and going and returns on a handy 25-day break from stall four, though his last three finishes outside the placings makes finding the line a concern.

runners_data.name: Ashford Hill
runners_data.note: A five-year-old exposed in this grade whose five runs on standard-to-slow turf show zero wins and zero places; Isobelle Chalmers claims 7lb but the gelding races back in a trip range (7f) where he has regularly finished mid-pack, and the style redistribution problem leaves him without a clear tactical route.|
runners_data.comment: Ashford Hill has shown she can compete at this level, with a third last time out and another third three starts back, yet she remains winless in her last six starts and that inconsistency is the concern; carrying 126 lb from stall three, she has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Blue Point Express
runners_data.note: Returned a win and two places from four runs on good ground in his history, though a 62-day absence is the longest break in this field and Adrian Wintle's yard is running at 1/14 over the past fortnight; dropped to 45 OR, the price could be interesting if he handles soft, but form away from good is untested.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and not seen for 62 days, Blue Point Express does at least bring experience of today's distance and going, though her recent form figures make for sobering reading and she faces a stiff task from a rating of 45.

runners_data.name: Pacific Prince
runners_data.note: Carries a B (brought down or refused) and two 10th-place finishes in recent form and has not won in ten soft-ground starts; James Bennett's stable is 1/1 in the 14-day window which is a small positive, but the "fades in finish" tag and 83-day absence make this horse a hard case to construct.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Pacific Prince also suffered a fall last time out after 83 days off — hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and carries a manageable 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Aplaceinthesun
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's three-year-old has finished 0-0 in seven and eight-furlong turf handicaps and is tagged as fading in the finish; Libby Swallow claims 7lb but the form string 08-740 offers little encouragement, and this horse will struggle to find the position that would make a difference given the redistribution.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Aplaceinthesun faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and a 20-day break gives connections some hope she returns refreshed.

runners_data.name: Snow Day
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's three-year-old has finished 6th, 6th, 8th, 14th and 12th in the last five, with three of those on going worse than good — the "fades in finish" flag is backed by a pattern of weakening well before the line, and Myla Coppins' 5lb claim cannot mask the absence of any realistic winning form.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with three finishes of sixth or worse and two unplaced efforts, Snow Day is hard to fancy on recent form, and our rating ranks her last of eleven; the experience over today's trip and a prompt 24-day turnaround are slim consolations.

runners_data.name: Margorie
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's four-year-old has a win and a place from three starts on soft or good-to-soft ground, which makes her one of the best-credentialled horses in this field for today's conditions; Callum Hutchinson rides and the headgear note (p) suggests the stable is looking for a positive response after a 41-day break.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Margorie nonetheless catches the eye with experience over today's trip and going, and her rating of 60 edges her official mark, suggesting she may be better than she appears; the risk is that her latest run ended in disqualification, adding uncertainty to an already patchy record.

runners_data.name: Nammos
runners_data.note: John & Rhys Flint's six-year-old is fresh off a 4th and a 5th from two recent runs at 8f on good ground and has won twice at 8f on Fibresand — the drop to 7f on soft is a slight query but the horse's consistency is the best in this field and Mason Paetel claims 3lb from a capable perch.|
runners_data.comment: Nammos is the top-rated runner on 64 and has experience of today's distance and going, which counts in her favour; she was a winner five starts back, though her last three runs have yielded a pair of fifths and a fourth, so a return to that form is the task at 134 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Ajrad
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's eight-year-old has four wins/places from fifteen runs and carries headgear (p); Lewis Edmunds rides and the horse's best form has come on good ground over 7-8f — a natural hold-up horse whose tactical options are compressed by the volume of closers here, though his experience means he may carve out a better berth than most.|
runners_data.comment: Ajrad shaped with promise when third three starts back and returns on a snappy 13-day turnaround having run over today's trip and conditions before; rated 61 by our assessors, he looks a lively threat from stall two, though he remains winless in his last six starts and will need to find more late on.

races.paceDynamic: Escape Magic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f handicap on Good To Soft ground at Chepstow, and with no genuine rival looking to push the pace from the outset, Rossa Ryan can dictate terms at a measured, energy-conserving tempo suited to soft conditions. The pace is sustainable rather than punishing, which historically compresses the field and reduces the advantage of coming from off the pace — horses racing prominently or just behind the leader will be travelling comfortably into the home straight without being stretched. This shape strongly favours horses that can sit within two or three lengths of Escape Magic and quicken from a good position, rather than true hold-up types who depend on a strong pace to close into. Critically, this field holds far more hold-up horses than can realistically race at the rear in any meaningful sense — Ajrad, Prince Ali, Aplaceinthesun, Blue Point Express, Pacific Prince, Snow Day and Ashford Hill are all natural hold-up types, but with so many of them and so little pace to run at, most will find themselves bunched in midfield unable to use their preferred tactics; of this group, Ajrad and Prince Ali, both carrying headgear and with shrewd enough pilots, are most likely to actually secure a workable position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Escape Magic Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Escape Magic bowls along unchallenged and sets a soft, rhythm-driven gallop that suits the horse directly behind.
scenarios.body: Rossa Ryan on the well-handicapped three-year-old sets a comfortable tempo on good-to-soft ground, and horses able to track closely — particularly Margorie and Nammos who have the class and going form — come to challenge without having faced a true test of stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough that the field strings out and horses who hold good positions in the first half of the race pounce entering the home straight.
scenarios.body: With a sustainable pace and soft ground slowing the tempo fractionally, horses settled in the first third of the midfield pack — where Ajrad and Nammos are likely to find themselves — get a clean run and grind past the leader inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades Late
scenarios.trigger: If Escape Magic is asked for an effort early — due to the field being closer than expected — and pays the price in testing ground.
scenarios.body: Soft going and a 37-day absence combine to undermine Escape Magic's stamina as the field closes, and a horse that has tracked closely throughout, such as Fullstop or Margorie, inherits the advantage in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely strong pace develops, burning off the prominent horses and leaving hold-up types with ground to make up in the straight.
scenarios.body: This scenario is unlikely given the redistribution — most supposed hold-up horses will not be in their natural deep position — but Nammos, who has course and distance form, could benefit if the race turns truly searching, while Prince Ali's soft-ground win earlier in the year gives him a small theoretical claim.

watchPoints.text: Escape Magic — watch whether Rossa Ryan settles into a truly uncontested lead or if the field crowds him early; if he is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged, his current form (back-to-back wins) makes him the race's single most dangerous horse.|

Margorie — headgear reapplied after a 41-day absence, with soft-ground form the best in the field; if she travels smoothly just off Escape Magic's pace, the combination of going suitability and fresh conditions could make her the most dangerous challenger in the straight.|

Nammos — most consistent horse in the field across recent starts and claims the services of an apprentice for a handy weight allowance; if the pace is genuine enough to set up a sustained finish, his staying profile over today's 7f on cut ground could prove decisive.|

Blue Point Express — the 62-day layoff is the longest in the field and Wintle's yard is in moderate form; watch the market for any confidence signal, as an unexposed profile on a first run on genuinely soft ground could cut both ways.|

Pacific Prince — a "B" code (brought down or refused) appears in the recent record and 83 days off the track alongside a fading pattern; if this horse dwells or misses the break it could cause interference in a field where the majority are already clustered in the same middle segment of the track.|

races.name: Runtech Ltd Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Marisitta
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a win over 6f on Good ground and fair recent form, but her natural hold-up style means she is genuinely at the back of the queue here — the race note is that she's tagged as redistributed to midfield, and on soft ground over 7f with this many closers, getting a clear run late is her challenge; William Carson a positive booking.
runners_data.comment: Marisitta brings distance and going experience to the table and is lightly weighted at 130 lb from stall one, but her recent form is inconsistent — a winner four starts back, second two starts back, yet fourth last time out after just 13 days off.

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran whose six runs at 8f on similar going show six placed efforts and a preference for prominent tracking — 61 days off is a query but he's handled soft before and slots naturally just off the pace here, which is a rare structural advantage in this field.
runners_data.comment: Consistent at this level, Eye Of The Water has finished third twice in his last six starts and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 56 marks him as a clear danger; the concern is 61 days off the track without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: It's A Mugs Game
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Joe Tickle's yard (winless in 14-day strike-rate) with limited form, only one run on soft and that a poor one; hold-up style suits this shape in theory but the form is too thin to trust, and 19 days since last run doesn't add confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, It's A Mugs Game at least has experience over today's trip and a 19-day break could aid freshness, though rated 8 of 11 on our figures he faces a stiff task from stall 4 carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Lady Margret
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends a four-year-old whose five recent runs all show double-figure or deep finishes on good-to-firm and standard surfaces; her natural closing style is further hampered by being mapped out of position, and the step onto soft is unproven — the headgear flag is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Lady Margret makes for a tough each-way proposition despite returning on a reasonable 17-day break and having run over today's trip; the bare form figures offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Grace Harris filly (5/20 in 14-day window, active yard) with consistent placed efforts at 8f on Good, but all her recent runs are at a mile on good ground; dropping to 7f on softer going is a change of context, and as a true closer now filling a mid-division slot, she needs a messy race to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, A Rose Adaay does bring distance and going experience to the table and an eight-pound pull between our rating and her official mark is a positive angle, though that eighth last time out is the concern heading in.

runners_data.name: Lady V
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with unknown style and just three runs, all on Good or Standard; 91 days off is the standout concern, and while Rossa Ryan is a strong booking, this horse has never encountered soft ground and has no form beyond 6f — significant unknowns.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and returning after 91 days off the track, Lady V faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip before and a rating of 53 leaves a sliver of room for optimism from stall two.

runners_data.name: Big Moonrise
runners_data.note: David Evans three-year-old (2/17 in 14-day window) with a placed run over 7f on Standard and some fair mid-table efforts; a true closer pushed into midfield, and Edward Greatrex takes over — the step to soft is unexplored but the Evans yard is in reasonable nick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Big Moonrise faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a sound 19-day break carrying 121 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Kaiko
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle filly (1/14 in 14 days) whose form reads as a non-stayer at 8f on good ground; a natural hold-up type forced into midfield, over 7f with soft in the ground — nothing in the form string suggests she can go close, and Laura Coughlan's 3lb claim helps the weight but not the underlying form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kaiko faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip before and returns on a sharp turnaround of just ten days.

runners_data.name: Vape
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old confirmed front-runner from John & Rhys Flint (1/10 in 14 days), who is the sole pace-setter in this race and carries top weight of 135lbs; the soft ground is a potential stamina drain over 7f for an ageing horse, but the uncontested lead is a significant structural benefit and her placed run on soft is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Vape nonetheless catches the eye with a fourth three starts back, and our rating of 65 puts him clear at the top of this field; returning on familiar distance and going terms after 13 days, he is the one to beat despite carrying 135 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Rovinia
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's four-year-old (4/12 in 14 days) is the most in-form runner in the field with a win and three consecutive seconds; her 7f form on Standard is excellent and she handles cut ground — a natural closer who should be able to settle just off mid-division and sustain a strong late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Rovinia arrives in fine nick — a winner last time out and placed in three of her four starts before that — and she has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a leading player from stall 3; the slight worry is whether 133 lb blunts her late effort.

runners_data.name: Angel's Call
runners_data.note: Nikki Evans five-year-old (1/4 in 14 days) with a win and a third at 8f on Good, plus a previous win; her 19-day freshness is fine, she acts on soft based on historic profile, and Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is useful — a genuine hold-up horse whose form profile makes her one of the most credible closers in the race.
runners_data.comment: Angel's Call arrives in decent nick after finishing third last time out, with a win two starts back boosting his claims, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the main risk is whether he can recapture that winning form with 131 lb to shoulder.

races.paceDynamic: Vape is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead from the off, she should be able to bowl along at a controlled, self-set tempo on this soft-ground 7f Chepstow straight. The going is Good To Soft (reported consistently across the card) rather than the declared Soft, which means the surface is testing but not stamina-sapping, allowing a front-runner to conserve energy rather than labour. Behind Vape, the field is dominated by natural hold-up horses — Rovinia, Angel's Call, Marisitta, Lady Margret, A Rose Adaay, Big Moonrise and Kaiko are all true closers, but so many of them cannot occupy the rear in a conventional sense and several will be pushed into mid-division roles they don't naturally seek. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and of those, Rovinia and Angel's Call — with the best recent form and highest weights — are best placed to secure a genuine tracking position with momentum into the final two furlongs. A controlled, uncontested gallop from Vape on ground that rewards staying power significantly favours horses who can settle just off the pace or in mid-division and sustain their effort through the closing stages — pure hold-up closers dependent on a fast early pace to generate their run are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vape Controls, Closers Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Vape dictates an honest but unhurried pace and the genuine hold-up horses find clear runs to close.
scenarios.body: Vape sets a metronomic gallop that keeps the race together until the final two furlongs, at which point horses with genuine staying form on cut ground come through; the soft surface rewards those who travel well through the race rather than those who need a true test of speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Vape Steals It Front
scenarios.trigger: If the field allows Vape a soft lead throughout and the pace is slow enough that her advantage becomes insurmountable.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to press Vape early, she builds a winning lead on the bridle, and the hold-up horses — many racing out of their natural position — find themselves unable to generate meaningful late momentum on the softish ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Eye Of The Water or Lady V slot in just behind Vape and benefit from a trouble-free run in a race where true closers are caught wide or too far back.
scenarios.body: The prominent runners who travel just off the pace avoid the positional chaos affecting the redistributed hold-up horses and hit the front at the right moment; the soft ground does not stop them as long as they have been shielded from early traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles The Race
scenarios.trigger: If the field bungles early positions, redistributed hold-up horses get shuffled further back than expected, and a messy pace creates a race won by a horse who finds gaps late.
scenarios.body: With so many natural hold-up types forced wide or mid-division, the race develops in an unpredictable shape where a single horse finding an unexpected seam of clear running can win from an unlikely position.

watchPoints.text: Rovinia's recent sequence of 1-2-2-2 makes her the form horse — watch whether she settles cleanly in mid-division behind Vape, as any traffic issues in the closing stages would be costly for the most likely beneficiary of this pace shape.

Vape carries 135lbs as a nine-year-old front-runner on soft ground over 7f — if she begins to tie up in the final furlong, the winner will already be on her heels, and any sign of her weakening sharply is the signal for the closers.

With five confirmed hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, watch for a congested middle pack leaving the stalls — any stumble or slow break from Angel's Call or Marisitta could cost them several lengths they cannot afford to give away in a race run at a controlled tempo.

Lady V has been off 91 days and has never raced beyond 6f or on soft ground — Rossa Ryan's market move, if any, would be the only reason to take her claims seriously, but blind faith in an unknown quantity at this trip and going is a structural risk.

Eye Of The Water is the only runner whose natural prominent style genuinely fits the map position — a 10-year-old off 61 days who has placed six times at 8f, his form at 7f is shorter than ideal, but he is one of the few horses who will actually race where he is shown.

races.name: LSL Racing Chepstow Mile Series Final Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Spirit Of The Bay
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for the Flint yard who has finished third and first at 8f on Good ground recently; course form is moderate (3/15 in similar conditions, no wins) and from the rear of the field in a strongly-run 17-runner race, getting involved will require everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out following a win two starts back, Spirit Of The Bay brings distance and going experience to the table and comes here on a quick enough turnaround at 25 days, though her inconsistent recent record — a seventh and two fourths also in the mix — suggests she'll need to find her best to make a mark from stall 10 off 121 lb.

runners_data.name: Auburn Avenue
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type, runner-up on his latest outing at 8f on Soft/Standard, but his one win in similar going conditions out of 15 runs is a concern on today's softer surface; Carson is a capable pilot but the horse will need to be produced late in a race likely to be run at a solid clip.
runners_data.comment: Auburn Avenue won two starts back but has since finished fifth, making her form inconsistent; she has run over today's trip and going, returns after 25 days, and her 121 lb burden from stall nine may not help her land a blow here.

runners_data.name: Thanos
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a smart profile — two wins and three places from five recent runs including wins at 7f and 8f on Good — takes a prominent pitch which is ideally suited to the likely race shape; 60 days between runs is the main question mark for Harry Charlton, who has a strong 14-day record.
runners_data.comment: Thanos won two of his last five starts, with a third last time out after back-to-back victories, and has run over today's trip; however, 60 days off the track raises fitness questions, and 121 lb from stall 17 adds further pressure on a mark of 74.

runners_data.name: Rating
runners_data.note: Front-foot performer for Grace Harris who won over this course and distance on Good and has placed twice from 15 runs in similar conditions; Ashley Lewis (claim) keeps costs down and the horse's prominent style fits the anticipated race shape neatly, even if recent form shows a slight tail-off.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's distance and going, but her last-six record also features three fifth-place finishes, suggesting consistency is the issue; drawn six carrying 119 lb, she brings live claims but may need things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Law Of Design
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a visor, whose last six runs have produced finishes of 5-5-5-9-5 on Good ground — consistent but not quite good enough; Ian Williams has had just two winners from 26 runs in the last fortnight, and the horse's tendency to fill mid-table positions leaves little margin for error.
runners_data.comment: Consistent fifth-place finishes dominate Law Of Design's recent starts, and while he returns on a quick thirteen-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, he remains winless in recent starts and must find improvement to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Moonhall Lass
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's four-year-old has genuine back-of-the-field instincts and won over 7f on Good, but in this 17-runner field she will almost certainly be shuffled into a more prominent position than she wants; the style mismatch (STYLE_FIT 0.93) is a real structural concern and tempers confidence despite encouraging recent form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 17 on our figures and drawn in stall 13, Moonhall Lass is hard to fancy at these weights despite a win three starts back; she has experience of today's trip and going, but consecutive fourths since that victory paint a modest picture.

runners_data.name: Too Much Trevor
runners_data.note: A genuine two-time winner on Good ground who races from the rear, but the sheer volume of hold-up types means he will likely find himself further forward than ideal; Grace Harris has five winners from 20 in the past fortnight, which is a positive, though the position he's mapped to here (midfield) is not where he performs best.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fourteenth of seventeen on our figures, Too Much Trevor is hard to fancy at the weights despite winning last time out; he was third two starts back but seventh three starts back, and stall fourteen adds further uncertainty for a gelding who has experienced today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Redhot Whisper
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's five-year-old is a bona fide hold-up horse who has placed four times in his last five runs at 8f, showing real consistency; with hg:h (hood) as an aid, he arrives 22 days fresh, but in a field of this size the distance he will need to make up from his true starting position is a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Redhot Whisper arrives in fine nick after winning last time out, with a placed effort two starts back and experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour; however, he carries 114 lb from stall one and his patchy earlier form gives rivals a foothold.

runners_data.name: Homeland
runners_data.note: Front-runner with a win over 10f and a place over 8f on Soft, so the conditions are not a concern; the handicap gap between Homeland (OR 56) and Revelance (OR 85) is substantial, and Zoe Lewis (7lb claimer) may find the opening exchanges uncomfortable against a classier rival who wants the same real estate.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our ratings, Homeland faces a stiff task from stall 12 carrying 114 lb, and a win in his last five starts hardly screams momentum, though he was third last time out and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: The Bureau Club
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Charlie Pike who has placed once from five runs, finishing second over 8f on Good last time; the hold-up/touch of pace profile (hg:ht) means this race shape is less than ideal, and the trainer's blank 14-day record adds no positive trigger.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, The Bureau Club arrives here in reasonable nick after 22 days off, and a runner-up finish last time out offers some encouragement; she has run over today's trip before, though ranked twelfth of seventeen on our figures, she faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Bobby Dassler
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who won over 8f on Good and has placed in soft conditions, so the going is not an issue; however, his true running style is from the rear and he has been mapped to midfield purely because the race contains more hold-up types than can all settle at the back — his best performances have come from well off the pace, which this race shape makes difficult.
runners_data.comment: Bobby Dassler has finished eighth, seventh, and seventh in his last three starts, making him very hard to fancy ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, though he does at least bring distance and going experience and a win in his last six starts to the table.

runners_data.name: Scarfo
runners_data.note: Has excellent placed form including a win at 7f and multiple places at 8f on Good, making him one of the more interesting hold-up runners on raw form; pushed into a midfield role he doesn't naturally occupy (STYLE_FIT 0.94), his ability to express that form depends heavily on how the race develops in front of him.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Scarfo is hard to fancy despite being placed last time out and having experience of today's distance and going; he carries 114 lb from stall eight, and at an official mark of 48 faces a stiff task against 16 rivals.

runners_data.name: Revelance
runners_data.note: The class act in the field at OR 85, a winner over this course and distance on Good with Rossa Ryan booked again; Ralph Beckett has six winners from 38 in the past fortnight and the combination of top jockey, top trainer and front-running style in a race this trainer has pointed him at is the most compelling single-horse angle in the race.
runners_data.comment: Revelance showed a sharp return to form when winning last time out and, having run over today's trip and going before, conditions look in her favour; drawn in stall five carrying 138 lb, she is taken to follow up off a lively 25-day break.

runners_data.name: Talis Evolvere
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's six-year-old takes a prominent pitch but his last five runs show finishes of 5-6-6-7-2, and the trainer has had no winners from 37 runners in the past fortnight — a concerning strike rate; his soft-ground form is acceptable (three runs, two places) but recent momentum is against him.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on our ratings, Talis Evolvere has run over today's trip and going and shaped with some promise when second in recent starts, but he is winless in his last six outings and a trainer without a winner in 37 attempts over the past fortnight is a concern.

runners_data.name: Nakaaha
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's four-year-old holds a mark of OR 78 and has won over 8f on Firm, with five runs in similar going producing no wins; a genuine hold-up type (hg:h) whose chance in Scenario C is real, but in the dominant race shape he faces a tough task making ground against a properly-run pace over soft ground.
runners_data.comment: Nakaaha arrives in fine heart after a second last time out, and a winner three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the weight of 131 lb from stall 2 may prove the biggest obstacle.

runners_data.name: Kodi Fire
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Charles Hills who has won over 8f and placed at the same distance in Good ground; only one run in similar conditions (no win) is slightly concerning, but the prominent style suits the anticipated race shape and Finley Marsh is a competent pilot on a horse whose form figures include a recent "1-2."

runners_data.name: Eutropia
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's four-year-old is a consistent prominent runner with wins at 8f and 10f plus multiple places at the mile trip; one run in similar conditions (one win, one place) is encouraging, and a 38-day break is unlikely to blunt a horse who has been in fine form — a straightforward fit for the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Eutropia arrives with a consistent recent profile — placed in three of her last four starts, including second two runs back and third last time out — and has experience of both today's distance and going. The main risk is 38 days off the track.

races.paceDynamic: Revelance and Homeland are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner handicap on Good To Soft at Chepstow, and with both likely to press for the lead from the outset, the pace will be genuine and sustained rather than tactical. Revelance, trained by Ralph Beckett and ridden by Rossa Ryan, holds the highest OR (85) and looks the dominant pace figure; Homeland, with a front-running profile but a markedly lower OR (56), will push for position under Zoe Lewis but is unlikely to match Revelance's class at the head of affairs. The resulting honest gallop over a flat mile on softening ground will stretch the field early and set up the race for horses with tactical speed who can travel into the race from a prominent pitch rather than for those who need to be produced from far back. This field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Moonhall Lass, Too Much Trevor, Redhot Whisper, Bobby Dassler and Scarfo are all genuine back-of-the-field horses who are unlikely to secure their natural position in a 17-runner contest with strong early pace; Revelance and Homeland are best placed to claim the front, with Thanos, Rating and Kodi Fire best positioned to track them. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off a strong pace on soft ground and quicken into the straight — hold-up horses face a significant structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace holds, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Revelance and Homeland push along at an honest clip throughout and the race is won by a horse tracking the early pace from second to fourth.
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop on Good To Soft ensures the field is strung out and horses with tactical speed who travel into contention off the pace-setters have first run approaching the home straight; the prominent brigade avoids the inevitable crowding that will affect the redistributed hold-up horses making ground from further back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner dictates, stays on
scenarios.trigger: If Revelance exploits his class advantage from the front, controls the tempo and is never seriously challenged, winning with something in hand.
scenarios.body: Rossa Ryan on the top-rated horse in the field can dictate on his own terms and ensure the pace is just honest enough to stretch rivals without burning himself out; his recent winning form over this course and distance profile and trainer Ralph Beckett's strong 14-day record give him a meaningful edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft ground slows pace, hold-up horses land
scenarios.trigger: If the Good To Soft ground proves more testing than expected, significantly slowing the tempo and allowing hold-up horses to close late.
scenarios.body: A slower, more attritional gallop would compress the field in the straight and give genuine hold-up horses Nakaaha and Redhot Whisper the opportunity to finish powerfully through tiring rivals; however, this is partially discounted because several runners tagged as true closers have been redistributed from the rear and are unlikely to get into their natural rhythm in this field size.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, midfield poaches
scenarios.trigger: If Homeland drops out early and Revelance is overhauled in the straight, creating a vacuum that allows a midfield horse to swoop through with a well-timed run.
scenarios.body: A pace collapse after an early duel would briefly scramble the race shape and open a gap for a horse like Too Much Trevor or Scarfo tracking in midfield; but this outcome relies on horses racing out of role delivering as if in their natural position, which the redistribution flags caution against.

watchPoints.text: Revelance (Rossa Ryan) vs Homeland (Zoe Lewis) — watch the first two furlongs to see whether Revelance comfortably takes control or whether the two front-runners burn each other up competing for the lead, which will determine whether this race plays to the prominent horses or eventually invites late finishers.

Kodi Fire and Thanos must be tracked in the early stages — if either gets a clean prominent position just off Revelance, they will be ideally placed for the scenario that suits the majority of the race shape analysis, and drifting wide or getting caught in traffic at the start would materially alter their chances.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Too Much Trevor, Redhot Whisper, Moonhall Lass, Bobby Dassler, Scarfo) — in a 17-runner field, watch for a mass of horses jostling for position in the first two furlongs; any incident or significant checking in that group could compromise several of them simultaneously.

Nakaaha is the one true closer whose form at this course and distance makes him worth monitoring from the rear — if the pace slows dramatically in the final quarter-mile, he is the horse most likely to emerge as the hold-up beneficiary rather than the redistributed types who aren't racing in their natural position.

races.name: Tom's Big Bike Ride Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Magna
runners_data.note: In career-best form with three recent wins at 5-6f on Standard ground, but today's soft conditions are a concern given a poor sim-going record (1 place in 15 soft/similar); Tony Carroll's stable has been active and Rossa Ryan is an upgrade in class, but the going question is the key factor.
runners_data.comment: Magna showed a third three starts back then back-to-back wins four and five starts back, so there is winning form to call on, but her last two outings have brought a seventh and a fourth, and the return after 35 days leaves a small fitness question alongside a stiff 139 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Control Room
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's confirmed front-runner with a win on Soft and two places in eight similar-going runs, giving it the best going credentials of the pace-setters; Edward Greatrex rides and this horse's 5f record is solid, though a three-way pace battle will test its stamina reserves on this ground.
runners_data.comment: Placed second two starts back and a winner five starts back, Control Room brings solid recent form into this, and her experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset; drawn in stall four carrying 138 lb, she rates the one to beat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: A veteran 7-year-old fitted with a visor, last ran just 3 days ago which is a notable freshness flag, and while it won a 5f Good race recently its last six runs at 5f on Good have produced mostly mid-pack finishes; Pat Dobbs takes over and this horse will look to dictate but has been out of the first two far more often than not at this level.
runners_data.comment: Level Up won three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with his 138 lb burden from stall one the chief concern after two below-par efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Savannah Smiles
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type with a wind operation (hg:p) who has winning form at 5-6f on Good ground, but soft ground has historically caught her out; Ashley Lewis claims 3lbs and the Grace Harris yard is in form (5/20 14-day), yet getting a clear run from the rear on a straight 5f with a contested pace is a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in her last two starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Savannah Smiles is hard to fancy at the weights, though she has winning form in recent starts, has run over today's trip and going, and returns after just 13 days.

runners_data.name: Connie's Rose
runners_data.note: Consistent placer for Grace Harris fitted with tongue-tie and a hood (hg:tp), recording four consecutive placed efforts at 6-7f on Good and Firm; stepping back to 5f on Soft with a 2-day turnaround is sharp freshness, and Callum Hutchinson needs to hold a prominent position without being caught up in the front duel.
runners_data.comment: Connie's Rose has been a model of consistency, never finishing out of the first four in her last six starts, including back-to-back thirds most recently, and she has run over today's trip and going before — the main concern is whether she can convert that reliability into a win, having gone without one in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Double Naughty
runners_data.note: Young 3-year-old hold-up type whose best form has come at 6f on Good, and soft ground with a drop to 5f are both untested negatives; Taylor Fisher rides for a trainer showing poor 14-day figures (0/4), and this horse will need the pace to completely collapse to reach the principals from the rear of the field.
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back, Double Naughty has run over today's trip and returns after 18 days, carrying 132 lb from stall six; the worry is that her last four outings have yielded finishes of sixth, sixth, seventh and ninth.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at OR 48 with a history of placed efforts at 6f — a natural hold-up racer whose genuine style is racing from the rear, though the packed nature of this field means it will not find its natural position; nine-year-old veteran for John O'Shea whose stable is cold (0/3 14-day), and the style mismatch tempers confidence in its ability to land this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Some Nightmare looks hard to fancy here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 13-day turnaround with a placed effort last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Control Room and Level Up are both confirmed front-runners and will fight for the early lead from the gates over this straight 5f at Chepstow, creating a genuinely contested pace on Good to Soft ground. Neither is likely to concede willingly, meaning the early fractions will be honest-to-strong rather than a dawdle, which on soft ground will place a premium on stamina and relaxed travel through the race. Magna and Connie's Rose will press from a prominent position just off the duel, with the hold-up horses Savannah Smiles and Double Naughty forced to work from off the pace. This race shape — a contested lead between two genuine front-runners on energy-sapping ground — strongly favours prominent racers who can sit a length or two behind the duel and pounce when the leaders inevitably tire in the final furlong; pure hold-up horses will find it difficult to generate enough momentum from the rear on this ground in five furlongs. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the map can accommodate, with Some Nightmare pushed into a midfield mapping though a true hold-up operator — Control Room and Level Up are most likely to actually secure the front positions given their confirmed lead styles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Control Room and Level Up burn each other off at the front and the leaders tie up inside the final furlong on soft ground.
scenarios.body: The early battle between the two front-runners drains both horses late, leaving them vulnerable to those who tracked patiently just behind; prominent types who cover the early pace without over-committing emerge best placed. Magna and Connie's Rose, sitting a length or two off the heat, are ideally profiled to pick up the pieces in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Duel
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners establishes a clear lead quickly and the other capitulates, allowing a solo dictator to control the tempo.
scenarios.body: A single leader setting their own rhythm on soft ground can conserve energy through the race and maintain momentum to the line before hold-up horses can close; Control Room's course form (1 win, 2 places) gives it a slight edge in this scenario. Level Up's headgear flag (visor) suggests it can quicken sharply but consistency has been an issue at this level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely scorching and the entire front rank wilts catastrophically, leaving a clear opening for late runners.
scenarios.body: Savannah Smiles and Double Naughty would need the leaders to completely blow up for ground to be made up in just five furlongs on a straight track; this is a low-probability shape because soft ground rarely produces the extreme pace collapse required over such a short trip. Some Nightmare, though mapped to midfield, is a true hold-up type and faces the additional challenge of racing out of its natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner fully commits and the pace is softer than expected, turning this into a bunched sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A moderate tempo would compress the field and produce a messy finish where tactical position and jockey judgment matter most; Rossa Ryan on Magna has the experience to react in a bunched finish. This scenario is the least likely given both confirmed front-runners have demonstrated willingness to race prominently.

watchPoints.text: Control Room and Level Up — watch the first furlong closely; if neither blinks and both commit fully to the lead, both face being beaten late on Soft ground and the race swings decisively to the prominent trackers.
Level Up — having run just 3 days ago, monitor in the parade ring for any signs of dullness or fatigue that could compromise its willingness to bowl along at the front.
Magna — the soft going record (1 place, 0 wins from 15 similar-ground runs) is a concrete red flag that must be factored against its excellent recent form on Standard surfaces.
Savannah Smiles — watch the draw and early positioning; as a hold-up type in a 7-runner 5f race with two front-runners, any traffic trouble or slow start will leave it with an almost impossible task.

Connie's Rose — a 2-day turnaround for a 7-year-old is worth monitoring closely at the start; if it breaks smartly and slots in just behind the pace duel it is ideally placed, but a slow break would negate its preferred prominent style.

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a win over 10f on good ground 7 days ago, returning quickly; soft going is unexplored territory and the step to 1m2f at Chepstow is a question, though the yard has a 1/12 T14 strike rate worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Liberate arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, giving her a sharp profile of late, and her experience over today's trip and going adds further substance to her claims; the concern is that 140 lb represents a sizeable burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ghost Story
runners_data.note: Has placed repeatedly in soft and standard going over 10f–12f (2W5P in similar going), and while naturally a hold-up horse, is being redistributed to the front as the likeliest pace-setter; her soft-going form is the strongest in the field and that is the primary angle here.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placing in recent starts, Ghost Story brings solid each-way claims here, finishing third three of her last four outings and fourth the other, with experience over today's trip and going an asset; winless in her last five, she remains one to side with from stall three on a solid 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Meet Me In Meraki
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type placed over 12f on good ground and proven at this trip, shown in midfield only because the field's rear is oversubscribed; Pat Dobbs is a composed judge of pace and the horse's recent 2nd over 12f on good ground shows class at the distance.
runners_data.comment: Meet Me In Meraki has been consistent in his last three starts — fifth last time, a second two back and a third three back — and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Stipulation
runners_data.note: Racing with a hood (hg:p) and a true hold-up operator shuffled forward in the mapping; best form has come over 10f on good ground and the soft going is a marginal concern given sim-going figures showing just 1 placing from 15 soft-ground runs.
runners_data.comment: Stipulation has run over today's trip and going, shapes with solid claims off stall one carrying 130 lb, and that runner-up finish last time out — his best recent effort — suggests he is building nicely; the concern is that he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Zambezi Magic
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran who has run well over 12f on soft before (2W2P in 7 soft-going runs), wears headgear (hg:h), and returns after 39 days; true closer placed in midfield by mapping saturation, but his soft-ground experience is genuine and relevant.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Zambezi Magic has struggled to raise his game in recent outings, and at a rating of 61 ranked fifth of six he faces a stiff task here; experience over today's trip and going, plus a return after 39 days, offer slim grounds for optimism.

runners_data.name: Staywitherjohnny
runners_data.note: Youngest-profile hold-up type in the field stepping significantly up in trip from recent 8f–9f runs; trainer T14 strike rate of 2/10 is encouraging but soft going over 1m2f at Chepstow looks a stiff ask, and the redistribution to midfield masks his naturally rear-running style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a ninth two runs back sandwiched around rare encouragement — a third three starts back — Staywitherjohnny has run over today's trip and returns after 23 days, but ranked last on our figures she faces a stiff task from stall six carrying 124 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Ghost Story is the lone confirmed front-runner and, despite being a natural hold-up type redistributed to the lead, will likely find herself setting a steady, uncontested gallop on soft ground over 1m2f at Chepstow — a genuinely sustainable pace scenario with no genuine rival willing to press her early. Behind her, Meet Me In Meraki, Stipulation, Zambezi Magic, and Staywitherjohnny are all true hold-up horses shuffled into a midfield mapping because the field is saturated with closers who cannot all get to the rear; Liberate is also a hold-up type arriving from 7 days off. The field holds far more genuine hold-up runners than can realistically race at the back, meaning the race will functionally resemble a bunched, moderate-pace affair with most horses tracking closer than their natural style dictates, compressing the tactical advantage of true closers. This race shape — a lone leader dictating an uncontested, soft-ground tempo with a field of hold-up types unable to spread out — most favours horses with demonstrated soft-going form, a proven ability to travel prominently when required, and the class to quicken off a steady gallop, making Ghost Story's ability to control and Zambezi Magic's or Meet Me In Meraki's soft-ground experience the primary factors to watch.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ghost Story Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Story settles uncontested on the lead and controls tempo throughout on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: Ghost Story, though racing out of her natural hold-up role, sets a relaxed pace that suits a galloping test on soft going at Chepstow, and with no genuine front-runner to challenge her, she can dictate margins and quicken when ready.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grind Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going slows the tempo enough that closers who track midfield can sustain a late run to the line.
scenarios.body: The steady pace on testing ground means horses with soft-going form who can travel in mid-division rather than trailing wide pick up best in the straight; Meet Me In Meraki's strong soft/good-to-soft record and Pat Dobbs's hold-up expertise become key.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits One Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Story sets too easy a pace and the field compresses, leaving a strong finisher to pounce late from last.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo on soft ground creates a sprint-finish dynamic, and a horse with a late kick who has been denied their natural hold-up berth suddenly gets the gaps they need in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Early, Stronger Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners push forward and create a genuine pace, rewarding the horse with the best stamina reserves on soft ground.
scenarios.body: A breakaway from the usual hold-up pattern forces a genuine gallop, burning off those out of role, and the horse who can stay and relax mid-race wins a stamina test.

watchPoints.text: Ghost Story's redistribution to the front means her true hold-up tendencies could see her drift back if any rival applies early pressure — watch whether she actually commits to the lead from the gates.

Meet Me In Meraki, Stipulation, Zambezi Magic, and Staywitherjohnny are all genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield; if they all try to drop in, the early order will be congested and jockeys may be caught wide or short of room rounding the bend.

Zambezi Magic's 39-day absence combined with age (9) and soft ground makes his readiness to peak first time out a watch point — Bernard Llewellyn has a 0/11 T14 record offering no recent confidence signal.

Liberate runs just 7 days after her last start — watch whether the quick turnaround shows in her early behaviour and whether Ashley Lewis (claiming 3lb) can settle her in the rear before making her move on the soft ground.

The soft going at Chepstow over 1m2f will stretch stamina reserves significantly; horses whose sim-going records show repeated placed efforts (Ghost Story 7/13, Zambezi Magic 7/15) are the ones with genuine fitness evidence for this surface test.
